title: Pleistocene glacial cycles
summary: Over the past 2.6 million years, large ice sheets in the Northern Hemisphere have grown and retreated many times. These cycles first ran at about 41,000 years, then between about 1.25 and 0.7 million years ago became strongly asymmetric 100,000-year cycles. One study explains the change by declining carbon dioxide and glacial erosion of soil. Ice locks up water, lowering sea levels and exposing land. The last glacial period ended about 11,500 years ago.

importance.justification: Repeated ice ages reshaped climate, sea level and the land surface across the whole planet.

related.because: The onset of Northern Hemisphere glaciation at 2.7 to 2.58 million years ago initiated the Pleistocene glacial sequence.
The Mid-Pleistocene Transition restructured the glacial cycles from 41,000-year to 100,000-year periodicity.
